newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Majority of company directors want Ireland in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Majority of company directors want Ireland in EMU.

text.p: Most Irish company directors believe Ireland should be among the first countries to join the EMU, a survey by the Irish Institute of Directors (IOD) showed.
The survey, published on Thursday, was conducted among 670 IOD members in October 1996.
It found that 91 percent of respondents believed Ireland should be among the first participants in the single currency while 87 percent felt Ireland should enter even if the UK stayed out.
The survey also showed that while 73 percent of respondents had considered the effects of EMU, they had not done so in depth.
"Their knowlege will deepen as the debate moves on and there is more analysis and discussion of the impact on Irish business," IOD director John Callaghan said in a statement.
Directors in all sectors of Irish industry were polled in the survey, which the IOD plans to repeat to monitor opinion on an on-going basis.
